abstract: Deep neural networks have achieved state-of-the-art results on many vision benchmarks. In this paper we introduce a convolutional architecture with attention mechanisms to improve object recognition in natural images.
We propose a reinforcement learning algorithm that combines model-based planning with policy gradients to solve continuous control tasks more efficiently than existing methods.
Large language models can perform complex reasoning tasks. We fine-tune a transformer on dialogue data to build a conversational assistant that answers programming questions.
Early detection of cardiovascular disease is essential to reduce mortality. Using electronic health record data, we train a gradient-boosted model to predict 5-year risk of heart failure.
Radiologists must review a large number of chest X-rays every day. We develop a deep learning system that flags images with a high probability of pneumonia for priority reading.
Continuous glucose monitoring generates rich time-series data. We present a sequence model that forecasts dangerous hypoglycemic events up to 60 minutes in advance.

Subscription services struggle with customer churn. We design a survival analysis model that uses product usage and billing history to estimate the probability that a customer will cancel in the next 30 days.
Online retailers need accurate demand forecasts. Our gradient-boosted trees model predicts weekly sales using promotions, holidays and historical sales patterns.
High-frequency trading algorithms react to market microstructure. We build a model that predicts short-term price movements from limit order book data.
Climate change is increasing the frequency of extreme rainfall events. Using a regional climate model, we simulate future precipitation patterns and quantify flood risk for a coastal city.

Urban heat islands cause higher temperatures in dense city centers. We analyse satellite temperature data and land cover maps to identify which green infrastructure strategies most effectively reduce heat.
Air quality sensors measure particulate matter across a metropolitan region. We train a spatio-temporal model to forecast pollution levels and identify neighborhoods with chronic exposure.
Social networks influence how information spreads online. We study retweet cascades on a microblogging platform and show that user centrality is strongly correlated with cascade size.
Classical music recommendation systems often ignore musical structure. We propose a content-based model that uses harmonic progressions and instrumentation to group similar pieces.
University students form informal friendship networks. Using survey data, we build graph-based models to study how network position relates to academic performance.
